In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high-current electric-discharge laser with a return current conduction.
a study of the influence of the parameters of the active medium of a photodissociating laser on the radiation characteristics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the iodine laser is an extremely useful source of coherent radiation in the 1.3-1.5 micron region.
the iodine photodiseociation laser has been demonstrated to have the potential of being a useful laser for high power, short pulse applications.
, in general, the results of this study are consistent with the theoretical model of the iodine laser proposed in [2] (see also [3]).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iodine photodiasociation laser pumped with high-current discharge with return current conductor is a promising source of coherent radiation in the 3–4-µm spectral range.
the iodine photodisociation laser can be operated in the visible region of the spectrum, the radiation energy is 0.2 J, the divergence angle is 2.5 mrad, and the pulse duration is 0.5 μs.
the iodine photodisso-ciation laser pumped by radiation of a high-current discharge has a number of advantages over the CO2 laser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser efficiency is higher in the case of the SF6 mixture.
the radiation energy of the iodine photodisociation laser can be significantly increased by using a mixture of CF3I–Xe and a high rate of coupling of electric energy into the active medium.
the use of mixtures of CF3I and CO2 or SF6 with Xe, Ar, Kr, or He allows one to achieve a high radiation energy and low divergence of the radiation.
